market_holds: Sealed baseline (18:08 UTC): spot $60.66, front-expiry (Nov 20) straddle 7.42%, event-implied move 7.23%, ATM spread 43% of mid so indicative only; 25d skew +5.4 vol points, puts paid. Seven prior prints median |move| 6.97%, last two +13.58% (Jul-26, Q4 guide +23% on the Meta VDP deal) and -10.41% (Apr-26, weak next-quarter guide). Last November print (FY26 guide given, in line with ~$1.42B consensus) moved +0.06%. Tape: $64.59 on Nov 12, then -1.5%, -3.9%, -2.3% to ~$59.7 intraday today on 2.4x-4x normal volume, against SPY -3.4% and QQQ -4.8% over the same three sessions (Yahoo bars), so about 2-3 points of the 6% slide is DLB-specific. Q4 consensus: non-GAAP EPS $1.19, revenue $368.4M (Earnings Whispers, page read today), Benzinga $1.14 / $371.9M; both sit below the company's $362-392M guide midpoint of $377M; whisper $1.26. FY27 consensus (MarketScreener, 4 analysts, undated, likely last refreshed after the 2026-07-30 print): revenue $1,467M (+3.3% over FY26 $1,420M), EBIT $339M (+12%), EPS $3.55. No analyst rating or target change found after Aug 2026, so FY27 numbers are ~3.5 months old. The line the stock trades on is the forward guide (next quarter in Apr and Jul; this print brings the first FY27 guide).
view: Q4 itself is close to locked: the guide was set after the large Meta video-distribution deal signed early in the quarter and with minimum-volume commitments landing in Q4, and the Street already sits below the guide midpoint, so a headline in-line-to-beat is the base case and will not decide the reaction. The reaction turns on the first FY27 guide, and three things lean that guide toward the conservative side relative to a consensus that still asks for +3.3% revenue and +12% EBIT. (1) The unit backdrop worsened after the company last spoke: IDC put calendar Q3 smartphone shipments at -22% y/y (2026-10-15, 'not yet reached the bottom', recovery pushed to 2028) and PCs at -20.1% (IDC 2026-10-08) / -22.4% (Gartner 2026-10-12); Qualcomm on 2026-11-04 called handset demand and memory costs near-term constraints. Dolby's own CFO said in July that mobile is by far the most exposed market, PC second, and that 'the longer this goes on' the more it flows into next year. (2) FY26 is flattered by the Meta signing and Q4 MVC timing, which FY27 has to lap. (3) This is the first call and first annual guide of a new CEO, Marc Whitten (appointed 2026-08-27, ex-Meta/Unity/Cruise/Xbox), and the board's 8-K of 2026-11-13 fixes his FY27 bonus at 100% of target regardless of results and adopts a new severance policy covering the four legacy executives (including the CFO), which reads like a board preparing for a reset or investment year rather than a raise. Against that: the stock rallied from $58 to $65 through October after the unit data was public, so the market treated the memory story as known, and it has now given back about 6% in three sessions on heavy volume with puts bid, so part of a soft guide is already being sold. Net: a modest lean down, nowhere near the bar for a call.
unpriced: Possibly the size of the FY27 reset: the FY27 consensus (+3.3% revenue, +12% EBIT) looks stale (no revisions found since August) relative to post-July unit data and a new CEO with a guaranteed bonus and every incentive to set a low first bar. But the pre-print slide and put skew show the market is already leaning this way, so the gap is small and not shown.

recommendation.reason: The deciding line is the first FY27 guide; post-July smartphone and PC data (-20 to -22% y/y), lapping the Meta signing and MVC timing, and a new CEO's first guide all lean it below a ~3.5-month-old consensus. But I cannot show the consensus has not already moved, the memory story has been public since mid-October with the stock rising through it, and the stock has already dropped ~6% into the print with puts bid. 58% is below the 65% bar.
recommendation.what_would_flip_it: An FY27 revenue guide midpoint at or above ~$1.47B with operating-margin expansion intact (or a new, larger buyback/dividend step-up from the $427M authorization), which after a 6% pre-print slide would likely produce a sharp bounce.

self_critique: The memory-driven unit collapse has been public for a month and the stock rose through it, so the market may already treat FY27 as a known soft year. FY27 revenue consensus of +3.3% is not demanding, and Dolby's mix is shifting to categories that grow regardless of handset units (auto Atmos, imaging patents, VDP with Meta recurring revenue). Dolby historically guides wide and near consensus (last November: in line, +0.06%). The stock has already fallen about 6% into the print on heavy volume with puts bid, so an in-line guide plus a buyback could produce a relief rally. The 'new CEO resets low' story is a general pattern, not a measured fact about this board.
approach_notes: P3's freshest-data-first pushed me into EDGAR submissions, which surfaced the Nov 13 bonus/severance 8-K and the CEO change: the most informative items here. P4 helped me avoid calling the memory story priced or unpriced without showing it, but the FY27 consensus could not be freshly dated, which left the view below the bar.
